title: Our Class Editing Chart
intro: Ms Rekha has put up a chart of editing symbols. Learn what sp, cap and p mean, then be the editor.

sections.title: Match each symbol to its meaning.
Circle True or False.

items.q: Editing means checking and fixing our writing.
The symbol sp means 'speak loudly'.
The symbol cap tells us a capital letter is missing.
The symbol p can mean a full stop is missing.

sections.title: These words are marked sp. Write each one correctly.

items.q: skool
frend
techer
pensil
hapy
buk

sections.title: Fix the mistake the symbol shows. Write the sentence correctly.

items.q: my bag is blue. (cap)
We read a story (p)

sections.title: Write one sentence. Check it for sp, cap and p.
sections.a: Answers will vary. Check spelling, the capital letter and the end mark.

sections.title: Write two lines about your Friday. Then check them.
sections.a: Answers will vary. Check spelling and capital letters.

title: The Lost Lunch Box Notice
intro: Wei has lost her lunch box and is writing a notice for the board. Check the punctuation (p).

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: The symbol p means a punctuation mark is missing or wrong.
A question should end with a full stop.
The symbol p can point to a missing comma in a list.

sections.title: Each sentence is marked p. Write the missing mark.

items.q: Have you seen my lunch box ___
It is green ___ round and shiny.
It has my name on the lid ___
Who took it from the bench ___

sections.title: Match each symbol to the sentence that needs it.

items.right: It was a gift from Nani.

sections.title: Fix the mistake the symbol shows. Write the sentence correctly.

items.q: Is it in the lost and found box. (p)
items.a: Is it in the lost and found box?

items.q: It had rice dal and curd in it. (p)
items.a: It had rice, dal and curd in it.

sections.title: Write a notice for something you lost. Check your punctuation.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I lost my red cap. Have you seen it? Check the end marks.

title: A Recipe Card for Lemon Rice
intro: Sahana copied a recipe from her grandmother. Look for wrong words (ww) and missing words (^).

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: The symbol ww means 'write well'.
The symbol ^ shows that a word is missing.
We use ww when a word is spelled right but is the wrong word.
The symbol ^ means the sentence is too long.

sections.title: These are marked ww. Circle the right word.
Write the word that is missing at ^.

items.q: Wash the rice ^ a bowl. Missing word: ___
Heat the oil in ^ pan. Missing word: ___
Add a pinch ^ turmeric. Missing word: ___
Serve it ^ a plate. Missing word: ___

sections.title: Fix the mistake the symbol shows. Write the sentence correctly.

items.q: Add for curry leaves. (ww)
Let it cool ten minutes. (^)
items.a: Let it cool for ten minutes.

sections.title: Write two steps of a recipe you know. Check for missing words.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. Cut the bread. Spread the butter on it. Check no word is missing.

title: A Postcard from Abu Dhabi
intro: Hugo is writing to his cousin. Learn two new symbols: // for a new paragraph and ? for does not make sense.

sections.title: Match each symbol to its meaning.
Circle True or False.

items.q: We start a new paragraph when we begin a new idea.
The symbol // means 'rub out this line'.
A ? next to a sentence means the reader could not understand it.
A new paragraph starts on a new line.

sections.title: These are marked cap. Write them correctly.

items.q: abu dhabi
sunday
yas island
uncle faisal
august
hugo

sections.title: These are marked ?. Put the words in order so they make sense.

items.q: beach the to went We.
big was mosque The very.

sections.title: Write a postcard in two lines. Ask a friend if it makes sense.
sections.a: Answers will vary. Check that each sentence makes sense and has capital letters.

the seed grew in six days.

I could here it crying. The right word is ___.
It hid under a blew car. The right word is ___.
Its fur was as white as flower. The right word is ___.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: When a story moves from morning to night, a new paragraph is a good idea.
Every sentence needs its own paragraph.
We put // where the new paragraph should begin.

sections.title: Fix the mistake the symbol shows. Write the sentence correctly.

items.q: The puppy runned to its owner. (gr)
items.a: The puppy ran to its owner.

items.q: puppy The home went happily. (?)
